chunks: And by this chain, he said, Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:
When you perform part of your Ablution (Wudhu), so a need arises for you until your Ablution (Wudhu) dries up, so repeat your Ablution (Wudhu), for the Ablution (Wudhu) cannot be in parts.

key_terms.يَتَبَعَّضُ: To be divided into parts / to be partial
key_terms.يَنْشَفَ: Dries up (referring to the moisture on the body)

ai.seo_question: What should one do if their Ablution dries up before completion?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that if the moisture on washed limbs dries during an interruption, the Ablution is invalidated because it is not a cumulative act where parts can be preserved independently. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of *ittisal* (continuity), ensuring the ritual purity is performed as a unified, uninterrupted whole rather than a series of disjointed actions. This emphasis on continuity underscores the spiritual integrity required in acts of worship within the Ja'fari school of thought.
